descriptive_addition_not_registered.arm: ammonix_ornith: the shipped system (Ammonix decides, fine-tuned Ornith 9B writes), run on the same draw after the registered arms at the user's request
descriptive_addition_not_registered.note: decisions are identical to ammonix_gpt6 by construction (the decision path never sees the writer); the 1.0-point success difference comes from payer paperwork rejections (17 vs 13) on a handful of claims. Report: rollout_ammonix_ornith_t103.json. The run crashed twice on infrastructure (a text-cache miss with the text server down, then a container-swap timeout, commit 94666284) and was rerun; all model calls replay from the prompt-hash caches, token counts preserved.

registered_decision_rule: ammonix_gpt6 wins or ties both GPT-6 arms on success_rate_v2 under the tranche-99 band (5.64 points), AND spends fewer total GPT-6 tokens than each GPT-6 arm

verdict.registered_claim: HOLDS: ammonix_gpt6 wins or ties both GPT-6 arms on success and spends fewer GPT-6 tokens than each

honest_notes: single draw: against the strongest GPT-6 configuration (tuned prompt + k=25 retrieval over the agent's own records) the success margin is a tie under the registered band, so the defensible claim is parity-or-better at roughly a quarter of the token cost, not an accuracy win; against GPT-6 without retrieval the accuracy win is outside the band
GPT-6 spent zero reasoning tokens under strict json_schema decoding; a chattier GPT-6 deployment would cost more than measured here
the ammonix arm's rerun replayed entirely from caches (writer calls_to_provider 0, cache_hits 565), so the crash recovery changed no model output and no token count
